page: Amazon Web Services c3.large is a third-generation compute-optimized instance operating on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, providing two dedicated virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. Memory capacity is set to 4.0 GB, which translates to 1.88 GB per core. The processor architecture includes a 25 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache. Instruction set coverage includes AVX and AES-NI, but excludes newer standards such as AVX2, AVX-512, and AMX. Storage is bundled via a 32 GB local solid-state drive, and no hardware GPU accelerators are attached.

Performance benchmarks position the instance within the lower percentiles across synthetic and application-level workloads. Multi-threaded evaluations show constrained throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 812.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 1640.98. Single-core performance is similarly limited, achieving 702.0 in Geekbench and 1263.58 in stress-ng. Memory subsystems reflect older architectural standards, with large-block uncached read speeds reaching 13.06 GB/s and write speeds reaching 11.39 GB/s. Application throughput tests demonstrate 0.73 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving rate of 1.81 GB/s.

From an architectural standpoint, the c3.large exhibits low compute and memory density compared to modern alternatives. While the integrated 32 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space without remote block storage overhead, overall throughput is bottlenecked by the single physical execution core and modest memory allocation. The instance represents an older generation profile with limited efficiency for demanding compute tasks, rendering it suitable primarily for legacy test environments, lightweight administrative utilities, and low-volume background workers.
